en.bio_html: My research focuses on spatiotemporal traffic data analytics, traffic safety modeling, and vehicle dynamics. I develop data-driven and physics-informed methods to address fundamental problems in transportation systems, including traffic state estimation, crash risk prediction, and driving behavior analysis. My work has appeared in Chaos, Solitons & Fractals, Expert Systems with Applications, IEEE Trans. on ITS, Physica A, and Transportation Research Part C, among others.

publications.title: Do traffic flow states follow Markov properties? A high-order spatiotemporal traffic state reconstruction approach for traffic prediction and imputation.
publications.authors: Hu, J., Hu, C., Yang, J., Bai, J., & Lee, J. J.
publications.contribution_html: Designed a high-order traffic state reconstruction method and proved the Markov property of traffic flow. Leveraged Markov matrix prior knowledge for high-accuracy traffic imputation under an auto-encoder framework.
publications.caption: Figure 1. Markov property-based high-order spatiotemporal traffic state reconstruction.

publications.title: A Simple Yet Efficient K-Nearest Neighbor-Based Method for High-Resolution Traffic Time-Space Diagram Imputation.
publications.authors: Hu, J., Bai, J., & Lee, J.
publications.contribution_html: Proposed a modified KNN framework for reconstructing Time-Space Diagrams from sparse data by matching spatiotemporal neighborhood features defined by Queen Contiguity Spatial Rule, with analytical error-propagation bounds derived via Green's function theory.
publications.caption: Figure 2. Efficient KNN-based high-resolution traffic time-space diagram imputation.

publications.title: Crash Risk Prediction Using Sparse Collision Data: Causal Inference and Graph Convolutional Networks Approaches.
publications.authors: Hu, J., Bai, J., Yang, J., & Lee, J.
publications.contribution_html: Created a crash data enhancement strategy utilizing historic spatial-temporal prior knowledge. Developed PST-CGCN — a novel method for crash risk prediction combining causal inference with graph convolutional networks.
publications.caption: Figure 3. PST-CGCN: crash risk prediction using causal inference and graph convolutional networks.

publications.title: Dynamic Correlation Analysis of Urban Crashes Using Tucker-Net Based SIRS Model: A Case Study in New York City.
publications.authors: Hu, J., Zhang, J., Bai, J., & Lee, J.
publications.contribution_html: Designed TNBSM, a data-driven and transferable model using tensor decomposition and the SIRS framework to explore dynamic crash correlations across urban zones.
publications.caption: Figure 4. TNBSM: Tucker-Net based SIRS model for dynamic urban crash correlation.

publications.title: Dynamic safety estimation of airport pick-up area based on video trajectory data.
publications.authors: Yang, J., Lee, J., Mao, S., & Hu, J.
publications.journal: IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems
publications.contribution_html: Assisted in designing a modified CUSBoost algorithm for imbalanced trajectory data classification, leveraging four risk indicators and spatial distribution analysis.

publications.title: Analysis of injury severity of single-vehicle and two-vehicle crashes involving lightweight vehicles (K-car) in Japan: A random parameters approach with heterogeneity in means.
publications.authors: Wang, L., Lee, J., Hu, J., Yang, Y., & Mao, S.
publications.contribution_html: Investigated K-car crash injury severity using random parameters probit models with heterogeneity in means. Designed an out-of-sample prediction approach to clarify heterogeneity among crash severity mechanisms.

publications.title: Contributing Factors to the Severity of Crash Injury and Vehicle Damage Involving Japanese Lightweight K-cars: Considering Unobserved Heterogeneity.
publications.authors: Wang, L., Lee, J., Hu, J., & Mao, S.
publications.contribution_html: Contributed to model design and analysis.

publications.title: Car following dynamics in mixed traffic flow of autonomous and human-driven vehicles: complex networks approach.
publications.authors: Hu, J., & Lee, J.
publications.journal: Physica A: Statistical Mechanics and its Applications
publications.contribution_html: Applied coarse-grained phase space analysis and complex network techniques to vehicle-following behavior, revealing distinct dynamical characteristics between autonomous and human-driven vehicles.
publications.caption: Figure 8. Car-following dynamics in mixed traffic flow: a complex networks approach.

publications.title: Vehicle dynamics analytics based on complex network techniques: a trajectory-based visibility graph approach.
publications.authors: Hu, J., Gao, D., Lee, J., & Wang, L.
publications.contribution_html: Introduced an adaptive trajectory-based visibility graph (TVG) framework that transforms planar trajectory data into complex networks, featuring a tunable visibility tolerance coefficient to capture maneuver-specific spatial scales.
publications.caption: Figure 9. Trajectory-based visibility graph for vehicle dynamics analytics.

publications.title: Rethinking driving style recognition: A prediction error-based driving behavior modeling.
publications.authors: Hu, J., Gao, D., Hu, C., Zhou, H., & Lee, J.
publications.contribution_html: Revisited end-to-end driving style recognition by exploring driver behavior heterogeneity through trajectory prediction model errors, and introduced a multi-modal distribution for future trajectories conditioned on driving style.
publications.caption: Figure 10. Prediction error-based driving behavior modeling for driving style recognition.

publications.title: Re-examining the explanatory boundaries of car-following models through fitting errors decomposition to uncover adaptive feedback.
publications.authors: Hu, J., Lee, J., & Wang, L.
publications.contribution_html: Posited that car-following model residuals are a composite of structural and random errors. Utilized an Unobserved Components Model to decompose residual series from three calibrated CF models, revealing adaptive feedback mechanisms that reduced RMSE by 15.8%–61.2%.
publications.caption: Figure 11. Decomposition of car-following model fitting errors and adaptive feedback mechanisms.

publications.title: Meta-learning guided by physics-based residual priors: a plug-and-play training strategy for lightweight car-following models.
publications.authors: Hu, J., Bai, J., & Lee, J.
publications.journal: Transportation Research Part C: Emerging Technologies
publications.contribution_html: Introduced RAMR, a plug-and-play meta-learning framework that reframes CF model training as a bilevel optimization task. Validated across four datasets with three physical models and three data-driven predictors.
publications.caption: Figure 12. RAMR: meta-learning guided by physics-based residual priors for car-following models.

publications.title: The Robustness Benefit of Disorder: A Global Typological Analysis of Road Network Morphology and Urban Performance.
publications.authors: Wang, L., Lee, J., Hu, J.*
publications.contribution_html: Using a global dataset of 70 cities, investigated how road network morphology (quantified by directional entropy) affects urban sustainability and resilience metrics including CO<sub>2</sub> emissions, commute times, and congestion.
publications.caption: Figure 13. Global typological analysis of road network morphology and urban performance.
